## Library Move Plan: Two Thousand Oak Street - Eight Weeks

This plan prioritizes preserving the local history archive and minimizing disruption to patrons. It assumes weekend-only volunteer availability and a single rental truck.





**Core Principles:**

*   **Archive Preservation:** Adherence to detailed archival practices.
*   **Sequential Sorting:**  Clear organizational flow to minimize chaos.
*   **Weekend Focus:**  Maximizing volunteer availability.
*   **Patron Communication:**  Maintaining clear updates on timeline and disruptions.


**Week 1:  Inventory & Archive Consolidation (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:** Conduct a detailed inventory of all items in the collection, noting accession numbers, dimensions, and any fragile items.  Pre-sort books into categories (Fiction, Non-Fiction, etc.) – this creates logical groupings for transport.  Begin preliminary labeling of archive containers (folders, boxes) using archival-quality labels.
*   **Archive Specific:**  Identify separate, climate-controlled zones within the new building for archive storage. Commence consolidation of the local history archive into standardized archival containers (acid-free folders, boxes). Label these meticulously and sequentially.  Prioritize fragile items for separate storage and careful documentation. 
*   **Volunteer Coordination:** Recruit 10-12 volunteers for weekend duties.  Assign roles (sorting, labeling, archiving assist).
*   **Resources:** Inventory software, archival supplies (acid-free labels, folders, boxes), labeling gun.
*   **Goal:**  Compile comprehensive inventory. Begin archival archive prep. Establish labeling system.



**Week 2:  Book Acquisition Sorting & Truck Prep (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:** Continued book sorting into categories. Develop a detailed packing checklist. Assess space limitations in the new building.  Definitive packing methodology determined. Start cataloging online/in situ to inform packing. Arrange for initial book transport planning. 
*   **Archive Specific:** Begin reinforcing fragile archival containers if needed.  Double-check labels on boxes for archive items.
*   **Volunteer Coordination:** 15-20 volunteers for book sorting and initial packing.  
*   **Resources:**Packing supplies (boxes, bubble wrap), checklists, online catalog (partial). 
*   **Goal:**  Advance book sorting. Finalize packing procedures.  



**Week 3: Archive Transport & Packing Begins (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:** Transport pre-labeled archive containers to designated storage areas in the new building. Begin systematically packing non-archival books, prioritizing frequently accessed items. Secure containers for transport. Pack heavy/fragile items with care.
*   **Archive Specific:** Ensure stable transport conditions for archive containers. Implement secondary barricades on containers.  
*   **Volunteer Coordination:** 12-15 volunteers for archive transport and packing.
*   **Resources:** Secure containers, packing tape, secondary padding (bubble wrap).
*   **Goal:**  Secure archive containment. Begin packing the majority of book collection.



**Week 4:  Intermediate Book Packing & Labeling (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:**  Continued packing of remaining books. Improve labeling of packing materials (e.g., “Fragile,” “Heavy”). Implement a staggered packing process.
*   **Archive Specific:** Review and reinforce archive labeling procedures. Test transport integrity of archived containers. Observe archival stability in new storage.
*   **Volunteer Coordination:** 10-12 volunteers to expedite the packing process.
*   **Resources:** Consistent labeling materials, packing tape, heavy padding, transport schedules.
*   **Goal:**  Pack intermediate categories of books. Confirm stability of archival storage.




**Week 5:  Truck Loading - First Phase (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:** Begin loading books into the rented truck.  Employ a “first-in rule” – placing items in a specified order within boxes aligned with packing order. Secure boxes during transport. 
*   **Archive Specific:** Continue careful transport of archived items. Ensure visibility of archive containers during truck loading. Monitor for shifting. 
*   **Volunteer Coordination:** 15-20 volunteers – a mix of book packers and archive assist. 
*   **Resources:** Truck loading equipment (dollies, ramps), securement straps.
*   **Goal:**  Complete first phase of book transport. Maintain archive safety during loading.



**Week 6: Truck Loading - Second Phase & Archive Placement (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:** Complete book loading. Transfer and place archived containers into designated locations within the new building. Double-check all remaining items are properly loaded.  
*   **Archive Specific:** Ensure correct placement of archived containers within climate-controlled areas. Verify access to archives. 
*   **Volunteer Coordination:** Primarily archive assist/support volunteers. Coordination with moving crew.
*   **Resources:** Truck loading equipment, specialized containers for archive movement.
*   **Goal:** Complete book transfer. Secure archival containers in designated locations.



**Week 7:  Emptying & Remaining Book Packaging (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:**  Empty remaining truck. Pack any final remaining items (office supplies, administrative materials). Ensure remaining containers are labeled correctly.
*   **Archive Specific:**  No archiving actions.  Archive containers remain where they are stored. 
*   **Volunteer Coordination:**  10-12 volunteers for packaging and cleaning.
*   **Resources:** Remaining packing supplies, cleaning supplies.
*   **Goal:** Complete final packaging. Create workspace for the new library.



**Week 8:  Final Sweep & Celebration (Saturday & Sunday)**

*   **Task:** Final sweep of the old building. Empty and clean all remaining spaces. Do a final inventory check. Document completed move.
*   **Archive Specific:** Verify archive containment stability. Confirm all archived containers are secured and protected.
*   **Volunteer Coordination:**  Remaining volunteers for final cleanup.
*   **Resources:** Cleaning supplies, final inventory checklist.
*   **Goal:**  Complete final cleaning. Document completed move.



**Ongoing (After Week 8):**

*   **Staff Training:** Train staff on new layout, access procedures, and inventory management.
*   **Patron Communication:** Continue regular updates on opening dates, new services, and layout changes.
*   **Archive Access Protocol:** Develop a detailed, regularly tested access protocol for the local history archive.




**Communication Plan:**

*   **Weekly Email Updates:**  Keep patrons informed of progress, any potential disruptions, and estimated timelines.
*   **Website Updates:**  Regular website postings for detailed information.
*   **Social Media:**  Announcements and updates via Facebook, Twitter, etc.
*   **Local Media:**  Press releases to local newspapers and radio stations.

**Contingency Planning:**

*   **Weather Delays:**  Schedule alternative weekends if adverse weather conditions prevent truck transport.
*   **Archive Damage:** Develop a contingency plan for handling any archive damage during the move. 



This plan provides a framework; meticulous tracking of labor hours, material usage, and potential issues will be necessary to ensure a successful move.
